# Code of Conduct

## Our commitment

DragonStrap is an open-source project. We want participation in the project to be respectful, constructive, and welcoming.

Everyone participating in this repository is expected to treat other contributors and users with professionalism and respect, regardless of experience level, background, identity, or point of view.

## Expected behavior

Examples of behavior that supports a healthy project community include:

- giving technical feedback constructively and with clear reasoning;
- respecting differing viewpoints and levels of experience;
- focusing discussion on the code, documentation, issue, or proposed change;
- accepting reasonable maintainer decisions and review feedback;
- keeping issue reports and pull requests relevant to the project;
- protecting private information, credentials, logs, and other sensitive data;
- helping make the project easier and safer for others to use and contribute to.

## Unacceptable behavior

The following behavior is not acceptable in project spaces:

- harassment, threats, intimidation, or discriminatory remarks;
- personal attacks, insults, trolling, or deliberately inflammatory comments;
- publishing another person's private or identifying information without permission;
- sexualized language, imagery, or unwanted attention;
- spam, repeated off-topic promotion, or disruptive issue/PR activity;
- knowingly posting secrets, credentials, private system information, or unsafe material;
- other conduct that is reasonably considered disruptive or hostile to the project community.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies to repository issues, pull requests, review comments, project documentation, and other spaces where someone is representing DragonStrap or the project community.

## Enforcement

Project maintainers may edit, hide, lock, or remove content that violates these expectations. Depending on severity or repeated behavior, maintainers may also restrict or block participation.

Enforcement decisions should be proportional to the behavior and focused on protecting the project and its participants.

## Reporting a conduct concern

If a concern can be handled safely in public, contact the repository maintainers through the relevant issue or pull request.

Do not publish sensitive personal information in a public report. If the matter requires private handling and no private contact method is currently published, avoid posting sensitive details publicly and contact the repository owner through an available private channel.

## Maintainer responsibility

Maintainers are responsible for clarifying these standards and applying them consistently and in good faith.

This project may update this Code of Conduct as the community and contribution process evolve.
